An anonymous source reports alleged new info about the GTA 6 review copies Rockstar sent to journalists:

- There are apparently no Xbox review copies because Xbox’s review process doesn’t meet Rockstar’s security expectations
- Reviewers weren’t given game codes. Instead, Rockstar worked with PlayStation to assign the game directly to a specific PSN account on a specific console
- Claims about gameplay watermarks are false and Rockstar is tracking potential leaks through a different, much smarter method
- Microsoft employees may still have access to Xbox copies for testing, certification, or other internal purposes, just not reviews
- Some Xbox content creators complained about not receiving Xbox review copies. Rockstar’s response was essentially: “Ask your Microsoft contacts why”

PSN security:
- Last month a group of hackers compiled a list of accounts they believed had access to the game but they were unsuccessful
- They reportedly managed to access one account but it was completely blocked from connecting to PSN when used on another console
- Rockstar and Sony have added extra security measures that link review copies to either an IP address or a console serial number
- If someone tries to access the account from a different IP address or console, it gets locked out and Sony is alerted

Yes, the green flame is caused by burning copper from depleting fuel in the regenerative cooling circuit and going oxygen-rich (closer to stoichiometric temperature) in the main combustion chamber. 

Slight underperformance of engines on this flight is the reason. The booster is meant to land with tiny residuals, so the solution is to improve engine performance and performance consistency (underway with Raptor V3.2), as well as adjust flight software to do MECO1 about one second earlier to ensure enough propellant for boostback and landing (tiny change).

These early ships and boosters are already outdated by improved designs in production or on the test stand, so this booster loss does not change our timeline to reach high volume, fully reusable Starship flights.
